prize_name: Frontiers of Knowledge Award in Economics Finance and Management
funding_share_basis: The purse is EUR 400,000 per category, paid entirely (100%, well above the >50% threshold) by the BBVA Foundation, the corporate foundation of Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, from the awards' creation in 2008 through the current (17th/18th) editions. The only other institution involved, the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC), contributes jury and evaluation-panel expertise but no prize money. The BBVA Foundation does not publish a breakdown of whether the money comes from a ring-fenced endowment or from the bank's annual budget line, but the payer of record is unchanged.
money_note: EUR 400,000 per category (plus a diploma and a commemorative artwork by Blanca Muñoz), paid by the BBVA Foundation since the awards were established in 2008; the amount has been unchanged since inception.
evidence_quote: The BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Awards consist of 400,000 euros, a diploma and a commemorative artwork in each of their eight categories.
judgment_reason: Coded Corporate because the BBVA Foundation is the corporate foundation of the single bank BBVA and is funded by it; the alternative is Philanthropy, since the foundation is a legally separate entity. A second ambiguity is the awarding body: the BBVA Foundation runs the awards "in partnership with" the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC), a public agency that co-appoints the evaluation support panels, so a coder could treat the award as jointly Government-administered. CSIC supplies expertise only and no purse money, so the BBVA Foundation is coded as both awarder and funder. Seat is Bilbao with a Madrid office, both in Spain, so country is unaffected.
